newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish government threatens press crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Turkish government threatens press crackdown.

text.p: Turkey's Islamist-led government on Tuesday threatened to restrict the secularist media which have played a key role in probing a security scandal that has shaken the governemnt.
"We want absolutely to bring the issue of lies in the media under control," Justice Minister Sevket Kazan told parliament.

"These issues are very serious. We are not at all complaining about the press supplying information. But it is necessary to take precautions about issues that even the media themselves complain about. We will have done the media a good turn," Kazan said during a debate on the media.

The debate follows a media probe into ties between the state and organised crime after a car crash two weeks ago in which a wanted gangster, a top policeman and a beauty queen died in the same car. A Kurdish chieftain who serves as an MP for the conservative wing of the government was also in the car.
The government says it is planning legislation to protect individuals from prying reporters and prevent biased stories as newspapers vie frantically to win the ratings war.
But Turkish secularist newspapers on Tuesday accused the government of preparing a censor law to take revenge on the press.
Turkey's Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan has been warning the secularist press for months that he will act against what he says is unfair and warped reporting.

Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller, a former prime minister and leader of the conservative coalition partner, has often been the target of corruption allegations in the media, which have also linked her to the latest car crash. The scandal has led to the resignation of the interior minister.

"Welfare wants to shut the press up completely. Welfare's ideology does not tolerate a free press," Zafer Mutlu, editor of the liberal Sabah newspaper, told Reuters. "And they are all afraid of the...scandals uncovered by the media."
